label: pp-clients-and-contracts
topic: Contracts: how a small team gets paid for a verified design pipeline
summary: Source-backed: SBIR/STTR is reauthorized to 30 Sep 2031 (Crowell); SBIR Phase I ceiling $335,937 and Phase II $2,239,578 without SBA approval (sbir.gov/about); awardees can keep title to inventions with a government licence (35 USC 202); universities usually offer an option to negotiate rather than an outright licence (UT System); Lean 4 and mathlib4 are Apache-2.0. Innovate UK 2026 terms could not be confirmed from a primary page. Pilot shapes, IP-ownership recommendations and price points below are general knowledge, not sourced. Not legal advice.
lay_summary: A small research team usually gets paid in one of three ways. It can sell a short paid study to a company, apply for a government innovation grant, or work through a university office that signs deals for it. In the US the main grant scheme has just been renewed until 2031, and early grants are in the low hundreds of thousands of dollars. A good first paid job is small: check one real design with the proof tool and hand over a report, like paying an inspector to certify one bridge before ordering a hundred. Who owns the proofs, the design files and the measurements must be written down before work starts. Free software parts used along the way come with a licence that allows commercial use but has a few attribution rules.

A secondary aggregator reports Innovate UK Smart-style rates of up to 45% of eligible costs for small firms in experimental development and up to 70% for feasibility/industrial research, and project sizes of GBP 100k-500k (6-18 months). Not confirmed for 2026; treat as unverified.

University sponsored research: inventions follow inventorship; an outright licence is not appropriate in a research agreement, only an option or first right to negotiate, usually royalty-bearing; 60-180 day periods are typical.

findings.claim: GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (unsourced): a Lean proof is a copyrightable text file; the theorem statement's truth is not owned by anyone. US copyright does not protect facts, ideas, procedures or mathematical concepts (Copyright Office Circular 33, read only as metadata; text not verified). Contract should name an owner or licence for proofs, design files and measured data separately.

GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (unsourced): a realistic first pilot is fixed-price GBP/USD tens of thousands, 2-4 months. Biomaterial proof of concept: client supplies the target spec; team delivers one formulation, measured mechanical/degradation data on N samples, and a short report, with milestone payments. Verification-as-a-service: client supplies one design and requirements, team delivers a formal statement of the property, a Lean proof or counterexample, a reproducible build, and a reading guide. No price was found in any fetched source.

recommendations: Run the first paid pilot as a fixed-price, milestone-paid, 2-4 month engagement through a sponsored-research or consulting agreement; keep it small enough to avoid grant timelines.

Use SBIR/STTR only if a US small-business entity (and, for STTR, a research-institution partner) exists; check the current agency solicitation for Phase I duration and size, which this run could not read.

Write three separate IP clauses: proofs and verification code (licence under Apache-2.0 or assign), design files (client owns, team keeps background IP), measured data (client owns the batch; team keeps rights to anonymised results).
Check each upstream dependency's licence and keep the NOTICE file; take legal advice before signing. Not legal advice.
